content.text:
The drawing is a benzene ring with three substituents: a nitrile (C≡N), a fluorine, and a nitro group (O2N).

Going around the ring:
- The carbon bearing the nitrile sits at the upper right.
- The carbon bearing fluorine is directly below it, so F is ortho to the nitrile.
- The carbon bearing the nitro group is at the upper left. It is separated from the nitrile carbon by one CH (the top vertex), so the nitro group is meta to the nitrile.
- Relative to fluorine, the nitro group is para: going from C-F around the ring through the lower-left CH and the left CH to C-NO2 spans three bonds.

This gives 2-fluoro-5-nitrobenzonitrile. Numbering the ring with C1 bearing CN, C2 bearing F, and C5 bearing NO2, the SMILES is N#Cc1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1F.

Atom check: the ring carbons are c1 (C-CN), c (CH), c(NO2), c (CH), c (CH), c1F. That is six ring carbons, with F on the carbon adjacent to the C-CN carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: N#Cc1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1F
